speakers.name: Tim Cook
speakers.title: CEO (outgoing; this is his final earnings call)

exchanges.question: Procedural: IR asks analysts to limit themselves to two questions and hands to the operator. No analyst question.
exchanges.answer: Asked callers to limit to two questions; no substantive content.

exchanges.question: How much of the roughly 500bp deceleration implied by 9%-11% September guidance is supply constraints versus FX, and what are the supply constraints that are broadening beyond advanced SoCs? Separately, are reported efforts to gain sourcing flexibility on memory about securing supply, mitigating memory inflation, or preserving the customer value proposition?
exchanges.answer: Parekh: September revenue growth of 9%-11% y/y is hit by FX (about 2.5 points sequential headwind to y/y growth from June to September) and supply constraints that increase significantly sequentially, affecting iPhone, Mac and iPad; together these get pretty close to the June total company growth rate. Cook: June constraints were primarily Mac, less so iPhone and iPad, driven by availability of advanced nodes for SoCs and less supply chain flexibility than normal; constraints are 'very significant' with limited flexibility to remedy. On memory: paid more in June than March (partly offset by carry-in inventory), expects higher memory cost in September partly offset by carry-in inventory and lower non-memory BOM costs; benefit from carry-in decreases beyond September, and market memory pricing continues to increase beyond September. DRAM has three suppliers, more would help supply and perhaps pricing; 'evaluating all options'.

exchanges.question: What adoption is expected for the Apple Upgrade program across the 2.5 billion-device base, and will it shorten replacement cycles for iPhone, Mac and iPad? Also, what has the iOS 27 public beta taught about Siri AI as an iPhone demand driver this holiday, and about compute costs and recovering them through iCloud+?
exchanges.answer: Apple Upgrade is a leasing plan offered in retail stores, not widely in all channels; Apple residual values are generally much higher than competitors'; uptake still to be seen but early feedback is quite positive. Parekh added it is only available in the U.S. right now. On Siri AI, developer and public beta feedback has been overwhelmingly positive; on compute costs it is early and Cook does not claim a complete plan, but there will be iCloud+ upgrade possibilities for heavy users. Did not address holiday iPhone demand or replacement-cycle impact directly.

exchanges.question: How much do supply constraints hit the December quarter, given the Street at about 8%-9% growth versus about 12% for September; any guidance beyond September? Could Apple broaden its silicon providers (the Arizona fab being built by another company) within a reasonable time to alleviate constraints?
exchanges.answer: Cook: the primary constraint is advanced nodes for SoCs; the root cause is a demand forecast issue, with iPhone (22% growth, also 22% year to date) and Mac (29%) far exceeding expectations; supply has been pulled ahead but there is a limit, and the September quarter will be one of scrambling on supply. Parekh: the 9%-11% reflects supply and FX; no color or guidance beyond the September quarter. On new silicon providers, Cook said this is not a partner or supplier issue and noted Apple sources over 100 million components this year from Arizona as part of the $600 billion U.S. commitment; he did not answer whether providers would be broadened.

exchanges.question: Is Apple pursuing multi-year LTAs with suppliers for supply at pre-agreed prices, and in pricing is the intent to protect product gross profit dollars or gross margin percentage? Separately, why did services growth of 12% come in a bit below guidance, why does September guidance imply a further deceleration (below 10% as reported), and is App Store pressure from AI reprioritizing time a factor?
exchanges.answer: Cook: Apple reluctantly raised prices because of a '100-year flood' on memory pricing with exponential increases; it weighs units, revenue and margin with a long-term view rather than a formula; LTAs not addressed. Parekh: services growth went from 16% in the March quarter to 12% in June, mainly FX, plus no F1 theatrical release this year (favorable in the year-ago June and September quarters) and App Store softness in mobile gaming; June roughly met expectations. Court ruling on U.S. link-out transactions remains in effect and the Supreme Court will hear Apple's appeal. For September, FX is a headwind of about 5 percentage points to y/y growth from March to September quarter, including another 2.5 points sequentially from June; AI reprioritizing time was not addressed.

exchanges.question: Has Apple seen any pull-forward of demand (consumer, enterprise, education) given memory pricing dynamics? Does AI at the edge open additional addressable markets over time?
exchanges.answer: Cook: iPhone has run at about 22% growth year to date and it is not obvious in the data that there is pull-forward. Apple has now raised prices on iPad and Mac and it is too early for a definitive conclusion on price elasticity because channel inventory and consumer response take time; more will be understood in the weeks ahead. On AI, there are enormous opportunities and running some percentage of requests on device is strategic and a competitive weapon; no specific new markets named.

exchanges.question: Will Siri AI change Apple's capital intensity given the mix of on-device, first-party cloud and third-party cloud? Separately, John Ternus is asked for a high-level view on a changing competitive landscape, including AI-device entrants such as OpenAI and SpaceX AI.
exchanges.answer: Cook: Apple uses a hybrid model with some third-party cloud and its own data centers; OpEx and AI spending have grown quite a bit, and COGS also carries AI expenditure. The cost impact of Siri AI is to be seen, with possible iCloud Plan upgrades from heavy use; the balance is uncertain. Ternus said there is so much opportunity in the space and Apple is focused on its plans; he did not address the named competitors or capital intensity.

exchanges.question: What are the hurdles and updated thinking for launching Siri AI in China and Europe? Separately, what drives the gross margin step from 48% (ex-tariff refund) in June to about 46.5% guided for September: FX versus commodity costs?
exchanges.answer: Cook: Apple is working closely with the EU commission and has not been able to launch everything simultaneously there; Siri AI is or will be offered on Mac in the EU since Mac is not covered by the same regulations as iPhone and iPad. In China, approval was received last week to ship the original Apple Intelligence features (such as cleanup), with more work required for Siri AI. Parekh: gross margin fell from 49.3% in March to 48.1% in June ex-tariff refund (120bp), and to the 46.5% midpoint of guidance ex-tariff (160bp); more than 100% of each change is explained by memory cost, partly offset by carry-in inventory, lower non-memory component costs and favorable mix, with FX minimal.
